entities.summary: Salvator Rosa is best known today as an Italian Baroque painter, whose romanticised landscapes and history paintings, often set in dark and untamed nature, exerted considerable influence from the 17th century into the early 19th century. In his lifetime, he was among the most famous painters, known for his flamboyant personality, and regarded as an accomplished poet, satirist, actor, musician and printmaker. He was active in Naples, Rome, and Florence, where on occasion he was compelled to move between cities, as his caustic satire earned him enemies in the artistic and intellectual circles of the day.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent Baroque painter and satirist, Rosa's flamboyant personality and works influenced artistic circles in Naples, Rome, and Florence, contributing to the development of Italian art during the 17th century. His legacy can be seen in the work of subsequent artists.
